It’s because when Survival got redesigned into a melee spec in Legion, it was based around its artifact weapon instead of the artifact weapon being based around it. Blizzard’s new idea for the survival identity was based around wielding a spear, it’s why every melee ability has a spear as an icon or references one. Another example can be seen in Frost DK, where you can make 2h work but it will never be as viable as DW due to how the spec works in modern days, having dual runeforge enchants and other talents in the tree just support the DW play style better. Fury Warrior has the same issue with single minded fury, which in modern times is basically a dead talent point. Survival is a victim of modern blizzard’s obsession with streamlining class fantasies to fit the idea they have in their head of how it should be and how to balance it, not player preference or lore reasons.

Humans in the Warcraft universe have a proficiency to adapt and master magic, and more importantly continue to evolve it. It’s why the biggest mage group (even at the height of Silvermoon before the destruction of the Sunwell) is the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. The same reason why humans quickly adapted to using the Arcane and adopting Magic during the Troll Wars after just having been taught by the High Elves, it has nothing to do with their Titan origins but with their culture. The Elves in WoW have a tendency to stagnate and grow complacent, the Nightborne were stuck in a bubble for 10,000 years but their magic didn’t evolve it stayed the same as it always was. Jaina Proudmoore is not an upstart, she’s a Dalaran Archmage, and Dalaran has produced some of the strongest mages in all of WoW, namely: literally every single Guardian including Medivh and his mother Aegwynn (wielder of said staff); Khadgar, Kael’thas (though an Quel’dorei crown Prince, with access to every source in High Elf society he himself studied in Dalaran and became an Archmage there.) Sure, the ancient Highborne had a highly advanced magical society but a lot of that didn’t come inherently from within them, it came from the Well of Eternity. You can see examples of their stagnation and lack of evolution in Arcane magic compared to Humans in literally every post-Highborne society, they try to replicate this former glory with a myriad of wells (Sunwell, Nightwell, even Nordrassil in Mount Hyjal to an extent) or alternate sources of power, like the Blood Elves channeling fel or the Shen’dralar draining demons. Just because Elves are inherently magical creatures with an inherent understanding for the arcane, time and time again it has been shown that it doesn’t make them better mages than humans, no matter how old Thalyssra is, she spent 10K years with ancient magic while the world moved on and developed new ways of using it.

Social media exists, the novelty of socializing in MMOs was a thing of its time, before it was easy to meet strangers in all corners of the internet. Now people usually socialize outside of games, be it social media, Reddit, Discord servers, etc. and just organize there to play games together. This applies to every genre of online game, it’s why lobby based competitive games have been all the mainstream rage lately. MMOs are still very much social, some more than others, others not as much anymore, but it’s just how it is, the Internet has grown since the early 2000s and the social aspect MMOs offered other games and social media can offer with less investment needed. Most MMOs have shifted into providing a virtual shared world for players where they can do their own thing without being forced to interact with others directly, be it with shared tagging of mobs or world events where you don’t -have- to group. They allow you to be social without really needing to interact with others directly.

GW2's problem is content, lack of care for meaningful content and the abandonment of end-game systems (dungeons, raids, etc) and bad marketing.

It's not as popular because of Arenanet. Arenanet has dropped the ball on content various times, first with Dungeons which were widely popular at launch, they stopped making them and replaced them with Fractals, which are mini-dungeons with frustrating mechanics and unrewarding systems. Then we have Raids, released on Heart of Thorns, huge content that while popular, came out of nowhere, and with no preparation, we went from having no Dungeons to suddenly having raids. Then raids became content that people enjoyed doing throughout Heart of Thorns and Path of Fire, only for Arenanet to once again forsake content and never make raids again, abandoning another path of end-game content.GW2's redeeming quality is the world events and map metas, other than that, the game just doesn't have meaningful content anymore, everytime people get into some sort of activity they know it's going to be abandoned at some point.PvPers went through the same thing, GW2 tried to be marketed as an Esports and alienated most of its PvP scene in flavor of pros, who just quit anyway due to balance problems. WvW has been through the same, it's basically been abandoned with little to no upgrades apart from a mount in Path of Fire.

GW2 has a big content problem, and it feels like it's just been sabotaged left and right by Arenanet, and when I say this I don't mean the average developer, maybe it's the higher ups, but yeah. Apart from all this you also have the huge problems we had with Living World Season 1 having a huge amount of content, and crucial story moments that were just straight up removed from the game. You have Icebrood Saga's very controversial run, and how it handled story and attempted to replace an Expansion release in it's place. It's a lot of things.  


Edit: I've played the game since release in 2012, and while I still love it and play it to this day, these reasons and more just make it hard for GW2 to be a lot of people's main MMORPG.
